title: deployment.set_target writes the durable target, adopting the orphaned admission module
description:
SPIDR child of task-04b3ce7e349743c2a156d32ee5550ba5, filed by architect-fa3a3e17 on 2026-09-06 on the governor's re-plan hand-back. That row measured at 18+ existing paths before its new files, past the 10-file cap, and the governor's note asks the split to "either adopt [deploy-target-contracts.ts] in the child that owns the constants or delete it from the worktree". THIS ROW ADOPTS IT.

WHY THE SPLIT FALLS HERE. `deployment.set_target` is an ORDINARY SYNCHRONOUS WRITE and `deployment.deploy` is not - bootstrap-contracts.ts:48 already records that distinction in its own comment. `CommandHandler` is `(context: HandlerContext) => ServiceOutcome` (bootstrap-ledger-vocabulary.ts:253), a SYNC type, so set_target fits GOAL_HANDLERS and deploy cannot. The parent keeps the async half.

THE ORPHAN THIS ROW ADOPTS. `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-target-contracts.ts` is UNTRACKED (`git status --porcelain` shows `??`) and `git grep -c deploy-target-contracts -- apps/daemon/src` returns ZERO IMPORTERS. It is not scratch work - it is a considered module holding the two kinds' vocabulary, the admission rules for an operator-typed target, and the aggregate the binding lands on, with its own header stating "ADMISSION IS A SECURITY BOUNDARY, NOT TIDINESS. Every field here is operator-typed text that ends up in an argv (`--network <network>`, `ssh <sshTarget> docker ...`) or on a receipt that a screen renders." That reasoning is worth keeping; an unconsumed module is not. This row gives it a consumer or the row is not done.

MEASURED AT HEAD (moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-fa3a3e17, 2026-09-06 - MOST OF THE ROSTER WORK IS ALREADY LANDED, so do not redo it:
- `daemon-command-vocabulary.ts:70` -> `"deployment.set_target": CAPABILITIES.GOAL, "deployment.deploy": CAPABILITIES.GOAL` (family table, DONE).
- `:361` -> both kinds in the operator roster, with `:358` commenting that deploy is served from an ASYNC entry (DONE).
- PAYLOAD_KEYS HAS MOVED TO ITS OWN FILE: `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-payload-keys.ts:165` -> `"deployment.set_target": ["environment", "network", "sshTarget", "url"]` and `:166` -> `"deployment.deploy": ["environment", "sha"]` (DONE). Plans naming PAYLOAD_KEYS inside daemon-command-vocabulary.ts are stale.
- `bootstrap-contracts.ts:51-52` -> both kinds listed (DONE).
So the roster is NOT this row's work. `git grep -n "deployment.set_target" -- apps/daemon/src` finds NO handler: the write itself is what is missing.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: adopting deploy-target-contracts.ts (tracked, imported, tested), the `deployment.set_target` handler in GOAL_HANDLERS, and the durable target aggregate that `deploy-ports.ts:32` already declares is "WRITTEN by `deployment.set_target`; only read here".

NOT IN SCOPE: `deployment.deploy` and its async entry, the journey, the roster counts - all the parent's.
definitionOfDone: `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-target-contracts.ts` is ADOPTED: tracked by git, imported by production code, and covered by tests. `git status --porcelain` no longer shows it as `??`, and `git grep -c deploy-target-contracts -- apps/daemon/src` returns a NONZERO importer count from a non-test module. An unconsumed module satisfies every existence grep while the feature does not exist.

`deployment.set_target` is registered as a SYNCHRONOUS handler in GOAL_HANDLERS (apps/daemon/src/goals/goal-services.ts), matching `CommandHandler = (context) => ServiceOutcome` at bootstrap-ledger-vocabulary.ts:253. It writes the durable target that deploy-ports.ts:32 declares is written by this kind and only read there. Do NOT add it to the async entries - it is an ordinary synchronous write and bootstrap-contracts.ts:48 already says so.

THE ADMISSION RULES ARE ENFORCED AND ASSERTED, because every field is operator-typed text that reaches an argv or a rendered receipt: a `url` carrying `user:password@` is REFUSED, and a `network` or `sshTarget` containing whitespace, a shell metacharacter, a newline or a NUL is REFUSED. Assert each with its specific code AND the layer that refused - never merely that it failed. The engine spawns with shell:false so a metacharacter cannot re-parse into a second command, but an unadmitted value still reaches a remote host and a credential still lands on every receipt.

THE DURABLE TARGET ROUND-TRIPS: written by the command, read back from a REAL store, with every member asserted. Setting a target twice for one environment REPLACES rather than duplicating - assert the read-back count is one.

NO ROSTER WORK. The family table, the operator roster, PAYLOAD_KEYS (now in apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-payload-keys.ts) and the bootstrap kind lists ALREADY carry both kinds - `git status --porcelain` proves daemon-command-vocabulary.ts, daemon-command-payload-keys.ts and bootstrap-contracts.ts are untouched by this row. Eight rows are contending those files; re-editing one is a collision, not thoroughness.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` covers no apps/** file, so say that rather than quoting a bare root count line.
taskRails: ADOPT THE ORPHAN OR DELETE IT - do not leave apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-target-contracts.ts untracked with zero importers. The governor's hand-back names this explicitly.
ADMISSION IS A SECURITY BOUNDARY, NOT TIDINESS. Operator-typed target text reaches an argv and a rendered receipt; a url with embedded userinfo puts a credential on every receipt.
SYNCHRONOUS ONLY. `CommandHandler` returns `ServiceOutcome`, not a promise. set_target fits GOAL_HANDLERS; the async entry is the parent's.
NO ROSTER EDITS. The vocabulary, payload keys and bootstrap lists already carry both kinds and eight rows are contending those files.
NO DEPLOY EFFECT, NO JOURNEY, NO UI - all belong to the parent task-04b3ce7e349743c2a156d32ee5550ba5.
